current_metrics.methodology_label:
Same-tenor cross-country breakeven inflation differential between
two countries' generic bond-implied breakevens at the same tenor
(e.g. US 10Y breakeven minus EUR-FR 10Y breakeven, US 5Y
breakeven minus UK 5Y breakeven).  Computed per-trade-date via
the SPREAD formula:

  spread_bps = breakeven_a_bps - breakeven_b_bps

where ``breakeven_a_bps`` and ``breakeven_b_bps`` are the spot
bond-implied breakevens at ``tenor`` for country_a and country_b
respectively (each computed by
``calculate_breakeven_inflation_simple`` constrained to that
country's own (nominal, linker) pair).  The two breakeven series
are aligned per-trade-date via a strict inner-join AFTER each is
computed independently; the spread is computed only on dates
where BOTH country legs have data (no synthetic spread points
are produced).

Sign convention is FIXED at country_a minus country_b — the tool
NEVER silently flips the sign.  If the caller wants country_b
minus country_a, they must swap the input pairs.

Cross-country construction by design: country_a and country_b
MUST be different sovereign issuers (e.g. UST vs FR_OAT,
UST vs UK_GILT, DE_BUND vs FR_OAT, FR_OAT vs IT_BTP).  Identical-
country pairs (e.g. UST/USD_TIPS for both legs) are rejected at
the schema layer — for same-country breakeven curve / spot work,
use ``calculate_breakeven_curve_spread_tool`` /
``calculate_breakeven_inflation_simple_tool``.  Inside each leg,
the (nominal, linker) pair must STILL share country and currency;
that same-country invariant is enforced by the underlying
``breakeven_inflation_simple`` primitive's
``_enforce_same_country_invariant`` helper which fires BEFORE
any market-data SELECT.  Leg-internal cross-country pollution
(e.g. country_a_nominal=UST + country_a_linker=EUR_FR_LINKER) is
refused with a controlled error envelope that this tool surfaces
with a leg-attributed prefix (``country_a leg failed: ...`` /
``country_b leg failed: ...``).

The output is a CROSS-COUNTRY INFLATION-COMPENSATION
DIFFERENTIAL, NOT a pure cross-country expected-inflation
differential.  Each leg's breakeven carries an inflation risk
premium and a relative liquidity premium between its nominal and
linker bond, and the cross-country spread inherits both at each
leg.

INDEX-FAMILY MISMATCH (load-bearing): different countries'
linkers reference DIFFERENT inflation indices — USD TIPS
reference CPI-U non-seasonally adjusted, EUR-area linkers
reference HICP ex-tobacco, UK linkers reference RPI (legacy
issues) or CPIH (newer issues), Canadian RRBs reference
Canada CPI.  These are NOT identical inflation references.
This tool does NOT attempt to harmonise indices (no
harmonisation is performed) because doing so would require
seasonally-adjusted / index-conversion metadata the repo does
not yet ingest.  As a direct consequence, a US 10Y breakeven
minus EUR-FR 10Y breakeven is therefore a CPI-U-vs-HICP
differential, not a pure expected-inflation differential; the
user MUST interpret the output with that index-family
mismatch in mind.  Use as a proxy for cross-country inflation
expectations only with the inflation-compensation caveat AND
this index-family caveat in mind.

time_series_spread.description: Cross-country breakeven spread (UST/USD_TIPS - UK_GILT/GBP_LINKER) at 10Y (breakeven_a_bps - breakeven_b_bps) over the displayed window.  Cross-country inflation-compensation differential; not a pure cross-country expected-inflation differential (carries inflation risk premium and liquidity premium at each leg, AND subject to index-family mismatch caveat — see the tool's methodology disclosure).

time_series_zscore.description: Rolling z-score of the cross-country breakeven spread (UST/USD_TIPS - UK_GILT/GBP_LINKER) at 10Y vs its own trailing window.
